investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-09T12:38Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production API's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at the /v1/agents endpoint. Because the failure is shared across every sibling check with the exact same error message, the fault is localized to the swarm gateway layer, not to any individual eval or check-specific code path.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service that the production API proxies agent provisioning requests to — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every call to POST /api/agents that requires remote agent provisioning received HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". Because the failure occurred before any agent was created, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) could be collected, causing the expected-output contract to be entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure availability failure localized to the swarm gateway; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the GitHub Actions workflow run history shows successful runs within the last 300 minutes and the published file's generatedAt timestamp is recent, the staleness is caused by a CDN/cache layer serving an old file rather than a missed workflow run.

If fetching https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json directly returns a snapshotAgeMinutes value <= 300, the eval runner may have received a cached or stale HTTP response rather than the live file, pointing to an eval infrastructure caching issue.
If the snapshot file does not exist or returns a non-200 HTTP status, the cause would be a deployment failure or GitHub Pages misconfiguration rather than a missed workflow trigger.

If a workflow run completed successfully but the snapshotAgeMinutes in the published file is still high, the age calculation logic in the snapshot generator or the statusSnapshotEvidence function in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs may be computing age incorrectly.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks the last successful run time of the GitHub Actions snapshot-publishing workflow via the GitHub API, alerting before the snapshot ages past the 300-minute threshold rather than after.
Add a warning-level assertion at snapshotAgeMinutes <= 180 (or another intermediate threshold) so the eval signals degradation before the hard 300-minute outage boundary is crossed.

Add an eval that monitors the GitHub Actions workflow run status (success/failure/skipped) for the snapshot publisher on each observability probe cycle, catching workflow failures independently of the published artifact's age.
Consider a canary eval that compares the snapshot's generatedAt timestamp against the eval run time server-side to detect clock skew or timestamp miscalculation in the snapshot generator.
